notes: Fights leave marks now. Sweat makes the skin actually shine, and a gassed or hurt fighter flushes red. Body shots dent the flesh, which wobbles back, and leave bruises right where they landed that go red, then purple. Bloody gloves smear blood where they hit, blood flicks off a cut face onto the chest, and a bad cut runs down the chest in streaks (it soaks into a shirt too). Big shots to the head can knock the mouthguard out, or a tooth, and it bounces across the canvas and stays there. Hoops players shine with sweat and flush when they're out of energy.
